I  The Atelier

Some garments deserve more than a repair.

There’s a moment at the final fitting when a garment stops being something you wear and starts being something that becomes you. We’ve been creating that moment since 1983.

Forty years at the bench teach a pair of hands what no pattern can. A shoulder is eased, never forced. A hem is measured with the shoes you’ll wear. And the finest work is the work nobody notices.

II  Services

Considered work,
across the wardrobe

Whether it’s a single hem or a couture gown that needs taking apart and putting back together, we look at every garment on its own terms. Every piece arrives carrying a story, so we treat the cloth with the same care that went into making it, from the first unpicked seam to the final press.

Occasion & Tailoring01 – 04

01

Wedding & Bridal

We fit your gown over as many sessions as it takes, and we like to start early, so the only thing you’re counting down to is the day itself.

02

Formal & Evening Wear

Black tie, evening gowns and the dress for that one particular night, adjusted to fall the way their designer always intended.

03

Couture Gowns

Designer and made-to-measure pieces, handled by people who understand the work that has already gone into them.

04

Tailored Suits

Sleeves, shoulders, waists and seats: the small adjustments that make the difference between a suit that fits you and one that simply hangs there.

Everyday & Repair05 – 08

05

Denim

Tapered, taken in or taken up, with the original hem kept, so your jeans still look like your jeans.

06

Leather & Suede

Jackets, skirts and trousers altered on machines built for leather, because a needle meant for cotton won’t forgive it.

07

School Uniforms

Hems and lengths kept tidy all year, with a little growing room tucked in. They will grow, after all.

08

Repairs & Restoration

Invisible mending, new linings, zips and buttonholes. The quiet work of giving a much-loved piece another ten years.

III  The Process

Three steps, unhurried

Fine work keeps its own pace. From the first pin to the final fitting, here’s how your garment makes its way through the studio.

01

Bring the garment

Bring the piece in, with the shoes and underthings you’ll wear with it. We’ll pin, mark and talk you through what the garment will and won’t allow.

02

Done in-house

Everything is done right here, by hand or by machine as the cloth asks. Nothing is sent away or hurried to keep a queue moving.

03

Try it again

You come back and try it on. If a line still isn’t quite right, it goes back on the table. It only goes home when it’s right.

“
The best alteration is the one nobody notices.
”
